faq.q: Why does a moving magnet make electricity?
faq.a: When the magnetic field through a coil changes, it pushes the electrons in the wire along. This is electromagnetic induction, discovered by Michael Faraday in 1831.

faq.q: Why does a generator use coils of wire?
faq.a: Each loop of the coil gets its own push from the changing field, and the pushes add up. More turns of wire give a bigger voltage.
asks: Why so many turns of wire?

faq.q: Why does a generator make alternating current?
faq.a: As the magnet spins, first its north pole and then its south pole sweeps past the coil, so the push on the electrons keeps reversing. The current flows one way, then the other.
asks: Do generators make AC or DC?

faq.q: Why is a generator harder to turn when the lamp is on?
faq.a: The current in the coil makes its own magnetic field, which pushes back against the spinning magnet. Energy is never free: the more electricity you take, the harder you must turn.
asks: Why does a generator get stiff?

faq.q: What turns the generators in power stations?
faq.a: Usually turbines spun by steam, water or wind. The generator itself works the same way in all of them: a spinning magnet and coils of wire.
asks: How do power stations spin generators?

facts: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831.
Mains electricity alternates 50 times a second in Europe and India, and 60 times a second in North America.

options.show: A changing magnetic field through a coil
options.say: A changing magnetic field through a coil

quiz.why: Only a changing field induces a voltage, which is why the magnet or coil must keep moving.

wrong.1: A still magnet gives a steady field, which induces nothing.
wrong.2: A generator makes electricity from movement; it needs no battery.
